evidence.label: An explicit obstruction to nuclear norm-ultrapower embeddings

headline: Proves, with a Lean check, an explicit C*-algebra that fits in no nuclear norm ultrapower, answering Kirchberg.
scope: Unital embeddings of separable C*-algebras into norm ultrapowers B^ω of nonzero unital nuclear C*-algebras, including the Cuntz algebra O₂.
plain: Every separable exact C*-algebra fits inside one universal algebra, the Cuntz algebra O₂. Kirchberg asked whether every separable C*-algebra at least fits inside an ultrapower of O₂, a much larger limit of copies of it. This paper answers no, with an explicit algebra built from a concrete group. The algebra does not fit unitally into the ultrapower of any nonzero unital nuclear algebra. Lean checks the main theorem.
doesNot: This does not settle Connes' embedding problem or the tensor-norm form of Kirchberg's conjecture, which are different questions.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Eberhard Kirchberg and N. Christopher Phillips, embedding of exact algebras into O₂
scorecard.significanceWhy: It answers Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem negatively with an explicit counterexample.

explanation:
Number the slots of an infinite list 0, 1, 2, and so on. Define one operator that moves slot n to slot 2n, and another that moves it to 2n + 1. Slot 5 goes to 10 under the first and to 11 under the second. Each operator keeps lengths, so it is an isometry. Together their images cover every slot exactly once, the even ones and the odd ones. That is the rule s₁s₁* + s₂s₂* = 1. The algebra these two generate is the Cuntz algebra O₂.

O₂ is surprisingly universal. Kirchberg and Phillips showed that every separable unital exact C*-algebra embeds unitally into O₂[1]. A C*-algebra is an algebra of operators closed under adjoints and norm limits. Exactness is a mild tameness property. The question is what happens without exactness. An ultrapower O₂^ω is a huge algebra built from bounded sequences of elements of O₂. Two sequences count as equal when they get close along a chosen limit, an ultrafilter. Kirchberg asked whether every separable unital C*-algebra embeds unitally into O₂^ω[2]. It is a different question from Connes' embedding problem[3]. The obstacle is that O₂^ω is very roomy. It even contains isometries that are not onto, so simple size arguments fail[9].

This paper gives a negative answer[4]. It takes vectors of three numbers whose entries are fractions with powers of 2 below. The group combines these vectors with 3-by-3 integer matrices of determinant 1 and doubling. Its full group C*-algebra does not embed unitally into O₂^ω[5]. The group does not depend on the target algebra or the ultrafilter[6]. It works for every nonzero unital nuclear target.

The inner part of the group, with integer vectors, has property (T), a strong rigidity condition[7]. Doubling sends it onto a subgroup of index eight[8]. For example, the vector (1, 0, 3) goes to (2, 0, 6). Integer vectors fall into 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 classes by the parity of each entry. Doubled vectors fill only the all-even class. The proof tracks finite-dimensional representations of the inner group inside a nuclear algebra. Only finitely many types can appear. Doubling would force an endless chain of new types, a contradiction.

How sure is this? A computer proof checker called Lean has a formal proof. It builds the explicit separable unital full group C*-algebra. It shows the algebra has no unital embedding into B^ω for any nonzero unital nuclear B and any free ultrafilter. No specialist review of the paper has been published.
hypeCheck: Major: it answers Kirchberg's embedding problem with an explicit example, and Lean formally checks the main theorem. No specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: An algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, closed under adjoints and norm limits.
The algebra generated by two isometries whose ranges split the space in two, like even and odd slots.
A tameness property: tensoring with the algebra preserves short exact sequences.
Well approximated by finite matrix algebras, in a precise sense; O₂ is nuclear.
Bounded sequences in B, with two sequences identified when their difference shrinks along a chosen limit.
A consistent rule for choosing which infinite sets of indices count as large, used to take limits.
A rigidity condition: representations with almost-invariant vectors have truly invariant ones.
The largest C*-algebra built from all unitary representations of a group.
